messages:
sara: Heads-up — spike on control-plane connectivity options for Private customers. Proposal: a regional fanout proxy that routes tenant traffic into customer VPCs via peering or TGW. Want quick triage on tradeoffs and a recommended default.

 tom: Quick summary from my side — two axes: connectivity (peering/TGW vs outbound-only agent) and tenancy (shared proxy vs per-customer relay).

 raj: Shared proxy is operationally simplest but increases blast radius and complicates per-tenant audit isolation. Peering adds route-table management pain (limits + churn).

 emily: From a compliance POV we should prefer a path that gives clear network boundaries for regulated customers. Shared proxy + peering makes KMS/audit separation harder unless we enforce strict tenant-level auth and logging.

 tom: Scalability note: VPC peering doesn't scale to thousands of customers in a region. Transit Gateway helps but costs and operational overhead spike. Outbound agent (agent -> our CP) avoids inbound peering entirely.

 sara: Agent-initiated outbound solves peering and firewall issues for customers, but it adds latency and makes in-region control-plane ops trickier. Any numbers on the latency delta?

 raj: We ran a mini-proto: agent -> regional relay (mTLS) adds ~10–15ms median in our staging workloads. Example call: `curl -H 'x-tenant: t123' --cert client.pem https://relay.rw-inference.internal/sync` We also saw stable connection churn with 60s keepalives; tuning helps.

 emily: Security notes: must use short-lived certs, tenant-scoped private keys, and per-tenant ACLs at the relay. Add token revocation + cert rotation cadence to threat model.

 tom: Recommendation idea: hybrid default. Mode 1 (default): outbound-agent for most customers. Mode 2: private-peering (TGW) for large enterprise customers who require low-latency SLOs. Mode 3: dedicated-relay (our infra in customer's account or dedicated VPC) for highest isolation.

 sara: Operational implications — need Console and infra-as-code templates so a workspace can pick its mode. Also need clear SLA differences per mode and rollout policy for upgrades/fallbacks.

 raj: Open implement question: multi-home failover. If regional relay A fails, agents should be able to fail over to B with sticky session semantics and a plan for KV cache invalidation. Also consider connection fanout limits on our relays.

 emily: I'll add compliance requirements: per-tenant audit streams, separate KMS keys for customer-managed encryption where required, and attacker scenarios for token/cert misuse.

 tom: I'll sketch network diagrams and a cost model (TGW vs relay egress) — TGW also changes IP addressing and needs NAT considerations for egress.

 sara: Action items: (1) I'll draft an RFC for hybrid control-plane modes + failover (owner: @sara), (2) @tom runs TGW cost/scale spike, (3) @emily does security/GDPR/KMS checklist. Please add anything else before EOD and I'll file the RFC.

 emily: :thumbsup: I'll include certificate rotation cadence and least-privilege ACL matrix.

 tom: I'll throw in a quick script to simulate N peering connections and route-counts.

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created branch `spike/ctrlplane-fanout` -> https://git.internal/redwood/spikes/ctrlplane-fanout

 sara: thanks — filing RFC later today. If anyone wants to pair on the failover details ping me in DMs.
